content:
Hi, I’m encountering an issue when importing both Mathlib and Physlib on version v4.29.0.

import Mathlib
import Physlib

This causes an error: import Physlib.Mathematics.Distribution.Basic failed, environment already contains 'Distribution._proof_1' from Mathlib.Analysis.Distribution.Distribution, while Cslib doesn't cause error.

Is Physlib supposed to be compatible with Mathlib when import same time?
Is there a recommended workaround?

@Joseph Tooby-Smith Is there a particular reason why Physlib redefines docs#TemperedDistribution (and names it Distribution)? I guess the Mathlib version is (a) specific to ℂ and (b) uses the topology of pointwise convergence. There is a comment that I remembered existing, but I've just found that it's not in the docstring, it's a literal code comment:

Since mathlib is missing quite a few results that show that continuity of linear maps and convergence of sequences can be checked for strong duals of Fréchet-Montel spaces pointwise, we use the pointwise topology for now and not the strong topology. The pointwise topology is conventionally used in PDE texts, but has the downside that it is not barrelled, hence the uniform boundedness principle does not hold.
Pinging also @Anatole Dedecker and @Moritz Doll.

emlis said:

Is Physlib supposed to be compatible with Mathlib when import same time?

In principle, yes, because Mathlib is a dependency of Physlib, but issues like this can arise (naming clashes) if no file in Physlib imports a deep enough file in Mathlib to witness the conflict. One way around this for the moment would be to import a subset of Mathlib or Physlib, instead of importing all of both.
Thanks, I’m going to try importing files individually and put imports in a single file to manage them.
It would be nice if we could import everything anyway. Isn't that the point of unified libraries?
this is why i pinged the relevant parties.
This is the kind of thing that should be possible to test, but we ran into weird CI issues when trying that in FLT#778. (I don't remember what went wrong, exactly, and the logs are gone.)
CSLib has an analogous test that I don't recall any issues with in CI. Mathlib itself has a test like this for its dependencies.

Both docs#Distribution and docs#TemperedDistribution specialise the field, but in an incompatible way and I have talked to Anatole privately that I want to change that. Using the bounded topology is a decision by physlib that I don't agree with, note that they can't prove continuity for most of their operations. There is not really consensus on what is the right topology, but using the bounded one requires way more functional analysis, which would block all of PDEs for no practical improvement (and changing it later should be very easy)

Why are tempered distributions only with reals: the main reason to use tempered distributions over classical distributions is the Fourier transform and so if you have a real tempered distribution you want to complexity to be able to Fourier transform. The only reason I can see is that the space of all real tempered distributions is slightly different than the space of all complex distribution, so some QFT construction that involves integrating over the space of tempered distributions might need it (thanks to @Michael R Douglas for pointing that out to me).

So regrading having distributions in Physlib.

Like Moritz said there are some reasons why you really need Tempered distributions over the reals. There is the QFT example, but also more basic examples in something like electromagnetism, you want e.g. charge distributions to be real not complex. We had distributions in before Mathlib did (I think), and given ours were defined with reals (which is what we needed) changing to Mathlib's complex distributions would be a change that takes away from the physics.

Regrading the topology, I don't have any strong feelings on this. I think pointwise convergence would work for our needs.

Nevertheless this is an annoying conflict. I think the easiest fix might be to:

  • Put distributions within Physlib in a namespace Physlib so it doesn't conflict interfere with Mathlibs.
  • Add CI to stop this happening again. @Chris Henson do you have an example of the corresponding workflow used on CSLib to prevent this?

(Maybe more generally though we should be putting everything in Physlib in the Physlib namespace. i know lots of conversations about this has happened with Mathlib, and seems like conclusion has also been not to).

There are two relevant things we do:

  • The test is just CslibTests/ImportWithMathlib.lean which imports both libraries. This is in a lean_lib target configured as testDriver, so if this fails our CI fails.
  • I wrote an environment linter Cslib.Lint.topNamespace intended to check that every declaration extends an existing top-level namespace, so will allow either extending Mathlib or strictly requiring that new declarations fall under our Cslib namespace. (I've noticed this is occasionally buggy though, either a mistake in the logic or some change related to modules)
Awesome, thanks Chris!

Chris Henson said:

CSLib has an analogous test that I don't recall any issues with in CI. Mathlib itself has a test like this for its dependencies.

You guys are clearly more CS-savvy than me! I added the test exactly when we had an import clash in FLT, and it has never worked. Can you point me to the test in CSLib?
See my first bullet above. FWIW it looks exactly the same as yours, just two lines to import both libraries. I don't understand what would be wrong, your PR seems fine to me...
Thanks for looking! I'll bump the branch when I'm at a computer and remind myself of the error (edit: actually it can easily be done on the GitHub app)

@emlis I fixed this specific issue in Physlib#1059. It still needs reviewed and to be merged with main. However, you might still be able to use it before then if you work on: 

rev := 91a62633c09ce0fa25a4c366247c8ee56e105c39

and the tagged version of Mathlib on v4.29.1.

Moritz Doll said:

Why are tempered distributions only with reals:

I think you meant complex here? I'm a bit confused, are you saying you are planning to incorporate reals and update the definition of docs#TemperedDistribution , or you'd rather just keep it as it is? I think ideally in Physlib we do want to use the Mathlib definition if it's compatible, so I'd like to make sure we understand what the plan is

edit: sorry I misread it, I think the situation is still the same then? Physlib has their own Distribution which is defined over [RCLike 𝕜] and maybe reconciling it with Mathlib's docs#TemperedDistribution when we want to do Fourier transforms is the way to go for now

Sorry, typo - wrote the message in bit of a rush. What I am thinking of is that both docs#TemperedDistribution (what you call Distribution) and docs#Distribution have the field as a variable, so that physlib can just switch to the mathlib definition

Together with would come a complexify operator that turns a real distribution into a complex one.
I was planning to do that at ICERM to discuss it with Anatole, because for some project I need to translate tempered distribution into classical ones and currently that does not work very well
Thanks, that would be ideal, looking forward to seeing how everything fits together.
